Stated Claim / Post Context:
Electric vehicles outsell fossil-fuel cars in Europe for first time, Angola bans single-use plastic, rat rangers

In today's edition: EVs outsell petrol and diesel cars in Europe for the first time, with electric car sales rising to 29% of purchases in August; Angola bans single-use plastics thinner than 0.05 millimeters as it tackles mounting waste; and rangers work to educate DC residents about ways to prevent rat infestations without using poison.

Actual Article Body:
Squirrel News Team | Posted on October 5, 2026 |

Photo: Zaptec/Unsplash (CC0)

In today’s edition: EVs outsell petrol and diesel cars in Europe for the first time, with electric car sales rising to 29% of purchases in August; Angola bans single-use plastics thinner than 0.05 millimeters as it tackles mounting waste; and rangers work to educate DC residents about ways to prevent rat infestations without using poison.

As high fuel costs, competitive pricing and government incentives boosted demand, EVs outsold fossil-fuel burning cars in Europe for the first time in August. EV registrations rose 52.2% year on year to 243,207 across 31 major European markets, while gasoline and diesel sales fell 23.4% to 202,931. EVs accounted for 29.2% of new-car sales, surpassing the 24.4% share of internal combustion engine vehicles.

Source: The Chosun Daily

Angola has banned the production, import and sale of single-use plastics thinner than 0.05 millimetres, effective immediately, as the country looks to reduce waste. The country generates about 4,560 tonnes of plastic waste daily and recycles less than 10% of its total waste.

Source: Plus News

Global life expectancy rose to 73.3 years in 2023, nearly returning to the 73.4 years recorded in 2019, according to the WHO’s latest Global Health Estimates. The data also show a continuing shift in causes of death, with communicable diseases accounting for less than half of all deaths in low-income countries for the first time in 2023.

Source: UN News

California has approved plug-in solar panels that connect directly to household outlets, letting residents generate their own electricity from balconies. The new legislation makes California the largest US state to permit the technology, offering households another way to produce power and cut back their electricity costs.

Source: Grist

A battery-swapping pilot in New York City is giving food vendors access to clean power without requiring them to buy or charge battery systems. The model could lower operating costs while helping sellers move away from loud, polluting generators.

Source: Canary Media

Climate Reserve is building a network to help climate researchers and projects continue after losing federal support. The group connects displaced workers with environmental organisations and seeks new homes for climate initiatives affected by the Trump administration’s budget cuts.

Source: Grist

In Washington DC, a group known as the Rat Rangers is teaching residents how to prevent rat infestations without using poison. The scheme followed a 2024 City Wildlife study that found many DC animals with blood-clotting problems had tested positive for rodenticides.

Source: NPR

Portland traffic officials are organising group bike rides from North and Northeast Portland to downtown during the weeks-long closure of southbound Interstate 5. The rides gives commuters an alternative way to dodge the disruption while travelling together by bike.

Source: OPB

The 22-compartment “AbortOmat” in Warsaw allows women to access the pills swiftly and anonymously using a six-digit code. The service was envisaged for those who cannot or do not want to wait days for mail delivery due to a missed miscarriage or health complications, or who worry about receiving the pills at home.

Source: The Guardian

England’s most important tern colonies are showing signs of recovery after being hit by years of bird flu, flooding and increasingly unpredictable weather, new figures from the National Trust reveal. The trust reported record numbers of little terns at Long Nanny in Northumberland, one of the UK’s most important breeding sites for what is the country’s second-rarest breeding seabird.

Source: The Guardian
